ve_generic: Vertical exaggeration (VE, slider 1-5x, default 1x, always displayed in the viewer) multiplies every height (water, seabed, reef) and never a plan distance: tan(apparent angle) = VE x tan(true angle). Every number on this page is a true (1x) value. Photo-match mode forces VE = 1.

models.name: Boscombe Surf Reef
models.state_short: As built, finished September-October 2009: idealised two-layer loft of the traced outline (2011-09-28 image) at the design crest +0.5 m ACD. The damaged April 2011 survey surface is an evidence layer only.
models.state_full: AS-BUILT 2009 (intact, finished Sept-Oct 2009): idealised loft of the verified outline with the design crest +0.5 m ACD. Evidence layer: April 2011 DGPS surface (after the container failure).
models.caption: AS-BUILT 2009 state (intact reef). Later: containers failed from March-April 2011 (one 70 m bag lost ~80 t of sand, 2 m crest dip), closed 31 Mar 2011, repairs never completed, ASR liquidated Sept 2012, site re-branded for diving/snorkelling 2014/2017; the bags still lie on the seabed in damaged form and still show as a shoal on the Navionics chart. Not modelled as a second state.

confidence.reason: Outline (2011 satellite), seabed (April 2011 DGPS plot, +-0.2 m colour read) and the as-built crest (designers +0.5 m ACD, Oct 2009 survey +0.45..0.65) are all sourced and agree, and Garmin Navionics shows the same shoal; but the zero of the survey plot (chart datum) is assumed (+-1.4 m if wrong), the as-built flanks and flat crest are an idealised loft, and the beach and ground under the reef are interpolated.
confidence.reason_short: Outline (2011 satellite), seabed (April 2011 DGPS plot) and the as-built crest (designers +0.5 m ACD; Oct 2009 profiles) are sourced and agree, and Navionics shows the same shoal; but the survey zero (chart datum) is assumed (+-1.4 m on absolute heights if wrong) and the flanks and flat crest are an idealised loft.

models.ve_note: A 1:3 flank (18.4 deg) looks like 33.7 deg at VE = 2 and 59 deg at VE = 5.

provenance.method: Outer edge of the dark bag field traced on Esri Wayback 2011-09-28; converted to the canonical frame (x alongshore, y offshore); drawn state = reef after the April 2011 damage
provenance.uncertainty: +-1 m on W/E/S edges, +-1.1 m on the shoreward edge; survey relief>1 m footprint is within 1-5% of the outline area (IoU 0.90, no shift)

provenance.method: Colour of each pixel of Fig. 9 (left map) -> nearest colour of the printed bar (+0.9 .. -5.3 m); map axes (OSGB36 gridlines) -> canonical frame via lat/lon and the S1 georeference; gaussian 1 m smoothing
provenance.uncertainty: +-0.2 m colour read; plot is itself an interpolated surface of DGPS lines (finer than ~3-5 m not trustworthy)

provenance.parameter: Vertical datum of the survey plot
provenance.method: Crest and depth values agree with the designers' ACD figures; Rendle's text calls the zero 'MSL ... Chart Datum, Newlyn' (garbled); EMODnet check. Viewer switch shows the alternative (survey zero = ODN ~ MSL)
provenance.uncertainty: +-1.4 m on ALL absolute heights if the alternative is true (relief unaffected)

provenance.method: Bournemouth chart datum is 1.40 m below Ordnance Datum (NTSLF); ODN ~ MSL; Mead Table 1 mean of four mean levels 1.375 m; gauge usual range centred +0.02 m ODN
Mead et al. (2010) Table 1; converted to the model frame by subtracting 1.40
provenance.uncertainty: +-0.05 m (table precision); tide gauge on Bournemouth Pier, ~1.5 km W of the reef

provenance.method: Quote: 'The design has a crest height of 0.5 m above chart datum'; settlement 0.5 m or less
provenance.uncertainty: design value; as-built/settled crest differs (see survey)

provenance.value: max +0.68 m ACD at x=20, y=193; median inside outline -1.20

provenance.value: median 2.3 m, max 4.1 m (survey); loft crest 0.5 - seabed
provenance.method: relief = surveyed surface minus thin-plate-spline seabed fitted to survey cells outside the reef

provenance.method: Fig. 9 across-reef section (62.2 m line): SW flank rises 2.0 m over 6-8 m (1:3 .. 1:4, steepest 2 m window 1:1.5); NE side 1:5 .. 1:7; map-derived median gradient is gentler (1:5.8) because the plot is smoothed

provenance.parameter: Seabed beyond the survey (beach y<100, corners, y>305)

provenance.method: surf line of the 2011-09-28 image between px (1300,772) and (1750,720); tide state at that moment unknown

provenance.value: x axis = bearing 83.4 deg, y axis = 173.4 deg
provenance.method: shape.json geo.shoreline_bearing_deg 83.4 from the georeferenced image (north-up Web-Mercator)
both after the April 2011 container failure; repairs began Aug 2011 inside the envelope (shape.json)
provenance.uncertainty: bag-field changes between April and Sept 2011 not resolved

provenance.value: AS-BUILT 2009, intact (idealised loft of the verified outline; crest +0.5 m ACD)
provenance.method: Lior's rule (2026-10-05): model the as-built state; later damage is NOT a second state. Loft: crest = design +0.5 m ACD (Oct 2009 DGPS crest +0.45..+0.65 m, Rendle & Davidson Fig. 9 lower panels), flanks 1:3 from the outline placed on the 1 m relief contour. The April 2011 survey surface (post-damage) is kept only as an evidence layer
provenance.uncertainty: crest +-0.3 m (design +0.5 vs Oct 2009 profile tops +0.05..+0.65, typical +0.2..+0.3), flank +-30%, flat crest idealised (design had a 'focus' and a 'wedge' section whose heights are not published)

provenance.value: drying patch 378 m2 (SonarChart) / 492 m2 (Nautical) vs survey >0 m ACD 296 m2; 0.5 m contour 950 vs 956 m2; 1 m contour 1630 vs 1609 m2
provenance.method: Colour fills of the Garmin Navionics screenshots (green drying, blue < 1 m) converted to canonical metres; compared with the zones of the April 2011 survey surface. Navionics shows the structure as it is now (damaged, not removed). Agreement at 0.5 and 1 m is within 1-2 %, so the same datum (chart datum) is very probable; it may also mean both come from the same survey (the viewer gives no survey date)
provenance.uncertainty: area +-10 % (pixel read, 0.38 m/px); datum of Navionics not stated; independence from Fig. 9 not proven

provenance.value: 16 soundings: mean difference model - Navionics +0.06 m, sd 0.49 m (in the survey area n=4: +0.41 m; extrapolated area n=12: -0.05 m)
provenance.method: 27 spot soundings + 6 contour labels of the Nautical Chart (z17) read by eye (scripts/navionics_reads.json), pixel -> lat/lon -> canonical; model seabed (ACD) sampled at the same point
provenance.uncertainty: read +-0.05 m (printed to 0.1 m) and +-1 m in position; Navionics data date unknown

provenance.value: semi-diurnal with double high water; MHWS-MLWS 1.76 m, max spring range 1.96 m
provenance.method: Water level slider LAT..HAT uses the six Table-1 levels (Bournemouth Pier gauge); heights above chart datum converted with z_MSL = z_ACD - 1.40. The double high water (stand) is not modelled: the slider is a static level, not a time series
provenance.uncertainty: +-0.05 m (table precision); actual level also moves by surge (+-0.5 m) and wave set-up

models.methods_html:
METHODS_3D - Boscombe Surf Reef (Bournemouth, UK): three-dimensional model

Note date: 2026-10-05. Model files: model.js, index.html, build_3d.py (regenerates model.js and docs.js). Frame, units and datums are defined in section 3.1. Every number below has a source line in SOURCES_3D.md.

1. Summary

The model shows the as-built state of the Boscombe geotextile surf reef (finished September-October 2009): the verified plan outline (4,042 m2, traced on the Esri Wayback image of 28 September 2011, which still shows the bag field clearly) lofted into a two-layer mound with a flat crest at the designers' +0.5 m above chart datum (ACD), 1:3 flanks, standing on a seabed read from the April 2011 DGPS bathymetry plot of Rendle and Davidson (2012, Fig. 9). Later events (container failure from March-April 2011, closure on 31 March 2011, aborted repairs, ASR liquidation in 2012, re-branding for diving in 2014 and 2017) are in the viewer caption and in section 3.10, not modelled as a second state. Garmin Navionics (accessed 2026-10-05) still shows the structure as a shoal with a 380-490 m2 drying patch at the right place, so the bags are damaged but not removed; its shoal areas match the April 2011 survey zones to 1-2 % at the 0.5 m and 1 m levels and 16 spot soundings agree with the model seabed to a mean difference of +0.06 m (sd 0.49 m). Confidence (3D): medium: outline, seabed and crest are sourced and mutually consistent, but the zero of the survey plot is assumed to be chart datum (the whole absolute height scale would shift by 1.4 m if it were Ordnance Datum, relief would not), the as-built flanks and flat crest are an idealised loft, and the beach and the ground under the reef are interpolated or extrapolated.

2. Data sources

Not used: any value from the Gemini folder; GEBCO (grid far too coarse for a 120 m object); the Plymouth PhD thesis of Rendle (blocked by a bot check, see REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR.md).

3. Methods

3.1 Coordinate frame and conversions

The model frame is the canonical frame of shape.json: metres, x alongshore (true bearing 83.4 deg, towards the east; Boscombe Pier is at negative x), y offshore (bearing 173.4 deg, the shore normal), z up. The origin is the point on the surf line of the 2011-09-28 image nearest to the reef centroid (50.719552 N, 1.839278 W; OSGB36 E 411442 N 91115). Heights are metres above mean sea level (MSL), z = 0 at MSL. The three.js scene uses X = x, Y = z, Z = y (right-handed, not mirrored).

(E1) Compass bearing of a canonical direction (dx, dy): bearing = 83.4 deg + atan2(dy, dx). True north in the frame is the unit vector (cos 83.4, cos 173.4) = (0.115, -0.993), i.e. north points mostly towards the beach (-y).

(E2) Image pixel (px, py) of S1 to canonical metres, with s = 0.37808 m/px (Web-Mercator ground scale at 50.72 N, 156543.034 cos(phi) / 2^18), origin pixel O = (1509.7, 747.8), alongshore unit u = (cos a, sin a), a = -6.59 deg, offshore unit n = (-u_y, u_x): x = s [(px - 1509.7) u_x + (py - 747.8) u_y], y = s [(px - 1509.7) n_x + (py - 747.8) n_y]. The 25 traced vertices are reproduced by the fitted 2 x 2 matrix to 0.006 m (the shared tool geom.py had a rotation bug, not used).

(E3) Web-Mercator: X = R lambda, Y = R ln tan(pi/4 + phi/2), R = 6,378,137 m; pixel = (X - X0)/(X1 - X0) W, using the bounds in the .geo.json sidecar of S1.

(E4) Fig. 9 pixel (Xp, Yp) of the left map to OSGB36 metres (gridlines read on the figure: E 411400 at Xp = 147.3, E 411550 at 433.5; N 91000 at Yp = 39.0, N 90820 at 235.3): E = 411400 + (Xp - 147.3)/1.908, N = 91000 - (Yp - 39.0)/1.0909; OSGB36 (EPSG:27700) to WGS84 with pyproj (Helmert, about +-5 m), then E3 and E2 to canonical metres.

(E5) Fig. 9 colour to height: the printed colour bar has ticks 0 to -5 m at bar rows 55, 93, 131, 168, 206, 244 px; the linear fit is z_survey = -0.02646 Y_bar + 1.455 (top +0.93 m, bottom -5.30 m). Each map pixel takes the value of the nearest bar colour (Euclidean RGB distance; median distance 11.7, 95th percentile 20 on a 0-441 scale); pixels whose distance exceeds 70 are rejected. Pixels hidden by the black section line on the left map are taken from the right map (the same surface, offset +469 px, -1 px by template match, SQDIFF 0.028), the rest inpainted (TELEA, r = 4 px). The colour bar saturates at +0.93 m, so crest peaks above it are not resolved.

3.2 Datums and tide levels

(E6) Chart datum (CD) at Bournemouth is 1.40 m below Ordnance Datum Newlyn (S4): z_ACD = z_ODN + 1.40. With ODN approximately equal to MSL (A4): z_MSL = z_ACD - 1.40. Depth below chart datum d_CD = -z_ACD; depth below LAT d_LAT = -(z_ACD - z_LAT,ACD) = -z_ACD - 0.06.

(E7) Water levels (S3 Table 1, converted with E6; model frame, metres above MSL): HAT +1.19, MHWS +0.81, MHWN +0.27, MSL 0 (estimated, A4), MLWN -0.23, MLWS -0.95, LAT -1.46. Check: MHWS - MLWS = 2.21 - 0.45 = 1.76 m, equal to the "1.76 m" printed in the text of S3; the mean of the four mean levels is 1.375 m ACD, consistent with the 1.40 m offset.

(E8) Cover over the design crest (+0.5 m ACD) at level k: c_k = L_k,ACD - 0.50: HAT 2.09 m, MHWS 1.71, MHWN 1.17, MLWN 0.67, MLWS -0.05 (dry), LAT -0.56 (dry). This agrees with S6, which says the upper section is exposed at low spring tides.

The tide at the site is semi-diurnal with a small range and a double high water (a stand around high water; S3 Fig. 1b "highly asymmetrical tide signal"; S11). The viewer uses a static level (slider LAT to HAT, buttons for each datum) and does not model the time curve, wave set-up or surge. Level source: Bournemouth Pier gauge, about 1.5 km west of the reef (S3).

3.3 Plan outline

The outline is the verified polygon of shape.json (S7): the outer edge of the dark bag field on S1, 25 vertices, area 4,042 m2. Its nearest edge lies 181 m, centroid 226 m and far edge 276 m offshore of the surf line (A1, A10). The model draws it as the toe line (magenta) and as the plan of the loft.

3.4 Seabed

The Fig. 9 grid (E4, E5) is resampled to a 1 m canonical grid by bilinear interpolation (no registration shift: a +-30 m search of the best overlap between the survey relief and the outline gives 0, 0 with IoU 0.90), normalised-convolved with a Gaussian of sigma 1 m, with the rim of the plot eroded by 2 cells. The plotted area is 23,500 m2 (y about 100 to 305 m).

The ambient (pre-reef) seabed S(x, y) is a thin-plate spline through the survey cells outside a reef mask (relief above a second-order polynomial > 0.5 m, plus the outline, dilated 5 m; cells decimated to a 6 m spacing; rim buffer 3 m): (E9) S(p) = a0 + a1 x + a2 y + sum_i w_i |p - p_i|^2 ln|p - p_i| (Duchon 1977; scipy.interpolate.RBFInterpolator, kernel thin_plate_spline, smoothing 2.0; Virtanen et al. 2020); the fit r.m.s. on the survey cells is 0.021 m. Inside the survey S = w S_survey + (1 - w) S_TPS with w = clip((d_rim - 2)/8, 0, 1); under the reef S = S_TPS plus the nearest ring residual decayed as exp(-d/8 m) (A8); outside the survey S = S_TPS (extrapolation, A10). The exported seabed grid is 161 x 191 cells at 2 m (x -160 to 160, y 0 to 380), z in cm, with a code per cell: 0 survey, 1 extrapolated, 2 interpolated under the reef. Beach cells (y < 100) are extrapolated; the model beach is not a measured profile.

3.5 Reef surface (as-built, default)

(E10) Idealised loft: r(x, y) = clip(r0 + phi/m, 0, H_c), H_c = max(z_c - S, 0), z_reef = S + r, with phi the signed distance to the outline (positive inside, metres), r0 = 1.0 m (the outline is placed on the 1 m relief contour of the survey, which gives IoU 0.90 with the satellite outline), m = 3.0 (run per rise, A7) and the crest z_c = +0.5 m ACD (design, A6). The flat crest plateau covers 1,780 m2; the mean relief inside the outline is 3.2 m. Volume V = sum r dx dy = 13,119 m3 against about 13,000 m3 stated (S3).

(E11) Evidence layer (not a reef state): the April 2011 survey surface z_surv = S + max(Z_s - S, 0) inside the reef mask, available through the "Reef surface" selector. It shows the container failure (offshore half of the axis at -0.8 to -2.8 m ACD, S2 profile: a 2 m crest dip and a trough of -1.1 to -2.2 m) and supplies the shoal-area comparisons in section 4.

3.6 Garmin Navionics reading (S9)

The old ChartViewer is gone; the Garmin Marine Maps page (title "Garmin | Marine Maps", footer "Not to be used for navigation") serves the Navionics Nautical Chart and SonarChart layers without login or CAPTCHA, and was used in an own headless Chrome (private profile, not the shared browser pane). Settings: chart type Nautical Charts or SonarChart Maps, depth units metres, shallow shading 1 m (blue = shallower than 1 m; SonarChart splits it into 0-0.5 m dark blue and 0.5-1 m light blue; green = drying, above chart datum). The Google Places search box gave no suggestions in headless mode, so the map was centred on 50.71753 N, 1.83891 W with the page's own Leaflet setView at zoom 16, 17 and 18 (18 is the maximum). Pixel to ground (E12): mercator metres per pixel 156543.034 / 2^z, pane 1000 x 751 px at screenshot offset (400, 113), centre (500, 375.5); validated against Leaflet's own latLngToContainerPoint to 0.5 px. Areas are pixel counts times (0.378 m)^2 at zoom 18; outlines come from skimage.measure.find_contours; positions go through E3 and E2 to canonical metres. Thirty-three soundings and contour labels printed on the chart (a digit with a subscript is metres and tenths) were read by eye from 3x enlarged crops (scripts/navionics_reads.json); position reading accuracy about 1 m.

Is the structure "ruined" for the Navionics rule? The bags were damaged (S2: one 70 m container lost about 80 t of sand in April 2011, an adjacent one lost by 2012; S12: repairs never completed, debris on the beach in 2017) but not removed: the 2025 Esri image shows a blurred patch with the same envelope (METHOD.md), and Navionics today shows a distinct shoal with a green drying patch at the shoreward-east half of the old bag field (centroid canonical (15, 209), 12.7 m from the survey crest zone). The offshore half is no longer distinguishable from the sloping seabed. Decision: the structure still exists and is recognisable, so Navionics is used for the seabed and as a cross-check of the shoal and the post-damage crest, but it does not set the as-built crest (that comes from the designers and the Oct 2009 profiles) because it shows the damaged state.

3.7 Viewer rendering

Seabed and reef are triangulated heightfields coloured by depth (seabed) or relief (reef). The water surface is a translucent plane at the chosen level L. Vertical exaggeration e (1 to 5, default 1, always displayed) scales all heights, including the water level and the datum labels: z_shown = e z, so the apparent flank gradient is tan(theta') = e tan(theta) (a 1:3 flank, 18.4 deg, looks like 33.7 deg at e = 2 and 59 deg at e = 5); distances in plan are never exaggerated. The photo-match mode forces e = 1. The survey-datum switch (A3 alternative) lifts the surveyed seabed and the April 2011 surface by 1.40 m against the water; the as-built crest is NOT lifted (the designers state it in chart datum, +0.5 m ACD = -0.90 m MSL), so under the switch the loft is rebuilt on the raised seabed, the relief shrinks by up to 1.4 m, the crest ends up under water at MSL, and the survey no longer matches the Navionics shoal lines (which are drawn in chart datum and never move). Camera parameters follow: heading as E1, pitch positive up, roll, vertical field of view, horizontal hfov = 2 atan(tan(vfov/2) aspect), 35 mm equivalent focal length f = 18 mm / tan(hfov/2).

3.8 Assumptions

  • A1 The outline traced on S1 (28 Sep 2011) is the as-built outer envelope; the envelope did not change between 2009 and 2011 (S7: same footprint in the 2025 image; the loss of containers lowered crest heights, not the footprint).
  • A2 Fig. 9 is a faithful, smooth rendering of the DGPS surfaces: features finer than 3-5 m are not trustworthy; heights are read to +-0.2 m.
  • A3 The depth axis of Fig. 9 is referred to chart datum (ACD). Evidence: crest in the Oct 2009 profiles +0.05 to +0.65 m against the designers' +0.5 m ACD; "225 m offshore in 2.7 to 5 m depth" and "3-5 m (CD)" match the survey seabed -3 to -5 m; S6: upper section exposed at low springs; EMODnet is 1.3-1.7 m deeper than the survey read as ACD but 3 m deeper if read as ODN; Navionics shoal areas match without a shift. The text of S2 ("MSL is equivalent to Chart Datum, Newlyn") is garbled and is not used. A switch in the viewer shows the alternative (survey zero = ODN).
  • A4 MSL = ODN within +-0.1 m at Bournemouth (S8: usual range centred +0.02 m ODN), so MSL is 1.40 +-0.1 m above chart datum.
  • A5 The Bournemouth Pier tide levels (S3 Table 1) apply at the reef 1.5 km east.
  • A6 As-built crest: flat at +0.5 m ACD along the whole outline (design value; the Oct 2009 profile tops are +0.05 to +0.65 m, typically +0.2 to +0.3, so +-0.3 m).
  • A7 Flanks 1:3 (run:rise), outline at 1 m relief. Source: the SW flank of the Fig. 9 across-reef section rises 2.0 m over 6-8 m (1:3 to 1:4, steepest 2 m window 1:1.5); the NE side is 1:5 to 1:7; the smoothed map gives a median gradient of 1:5.8. +-30 %.
  • A8 The seabed under the reef is the spline interpolation of the surrounding survey seabed; scour at the reef base (S2 reports erosion of the -3.5 m contour near the base) is ignored.
  • A9 Navionics depths are referred to chart datum (the viewer states no datum) and the shoal is the same structure; its survey date is unknown.
  • A10 Beyond the survey (beach y < 100 m, corners, y > 305 m) the seabed is a spline extrapolation; the shoreline y = 0 is the surf line of 28 Sep 2011 at an unknown tide.
  • A11 Static water level; no waves, set-up, surge or double-high-water time curve.
  • A12 The reef is a smooth 1 m heightfield: no container texture, no overhangs, the 54 containers are not individually modelled (layout unpublished).
  • A13 Pixel scale of S1 is the Web-Mercator ground scale at the latitude; checked against the 180 m pier (measured 167.5-178 m).

3.9 State drawn

AS-BUILT 2009 (default, Lior's rule of 2026-10-05). The "April 2011 survey surface" option is an evidence layer only. Differences are shown in the viewer as the crest-cover readout for both the design crest and the highest surveyed point.

3.10 Later history (not modelled; dated, sourced)

Date Event Source
2008-06 construction starts (lower layer 2008) S3, S12
2009-09/10 upper layer finished; Oct 2009 DGPS survey: crest +0.05 to +0.65 m ACD (state modelled) S3, S2
2009-11-19 official opening S12
2011-03-23 / 03-31 council inspection finds "substantial changes"; reef closed for safety S12
2011-04 DGPS survey: one 70 m container lost about 80 t of sand, 4 m gap, 2 m crest dip (probably a propeller strike) S2, S12
2011-08 repairs by ASR begin, suspended for winter, never completed S12
2011-09-28 satellite image used for the outline S1
2012 adjacent container lost, gap up to 10 m S2
2012-09 ASR Ltd liquidated (one source: Nov 2012); insurance settlement 2013 S12
2014-04 / 2017 site re-branded "Coastal Activity Park": diving, snorkelling, kite and windsurfing; surfing dropped S12
2017-12-26 debris from the decaying bags still washing ashore S12
2026-10-05 Navionics still shows the shoal and a drying patch S9

4. Validation

  1. Survey versus outline: area of survey relief above 1 m = 3,841 m2 against 4,042 m2 (-5 %); IoU 0.90 without shift. (An earlier IoU of 0.77 came from tracing the -2/-3 m colour edge, not from a registration error.)
  2. Volume: loft 13,119 m3 against about 13,000 m3 stated (+0.9 %); sensitivity (E10): slope 1:2 / 1:3 / 1:4 gives 14,184 / 13,119 / 12,161 m3 at crest +0.5; crest +0.2 / +0.8 gives 12,554 / 13,625 m3 at 1:3; r0 = 0.5 / 1.5 m gives 11,640 / 14,678 m3. So the stated volume is reproduced within the parameter ranges. The April 2011 survey relief volume is 9,573 m3 (damaged and smoothed). The designers' Fig. 3a design relief gives 11,540 m3 (project verification). The text "about 1 ha" would need 1.3 m of mean thickness, which does not fit two layers of 1-5 m containers; 4,042 m2 gives 3.2 m.
  3. Crest: highest surveyed crest point in April 2011 is +0.68 m ACD at (x 20, y 193) at the shoreward end; the Oct 2009 profile tops are +0.45 (across) and +0.65 (along the axis); design +0.5; Navionics: the shoal dries (crest at or above chart datum), no height printed.
  4. Datum (A3): crest and seabed pointers listed under A3; EMODnet (cells 115 m, relative to LAT) along x = 0: y 100-200: -3.99 m, y 220-320: -5.62 m, y 340-440: -7.05 m; the survey read as ACD gives -1.4 to -2.5 m and -3 to -4.8 m, so EMODnet is deeper by 1.3-1.7 m (older and smoothed grid); read as ODN the difference would be 2.7-3.1 m. Evidence favours ACD.
  5. Navionics areas (m2), Navionics versus survey zones of the April 2011 surface:
Level Survey (Fig. 9) SonarChart Nautical Chart
drying, above 0 m ACD 296 378 492
shallower than 0.5 m 956 950 -
shallower than 1 m 1,609 1,630 2,073

The drying-patch centroid is 12.7 m from the survey zone centroid. The close match at 0.5 and 1 m supports the same datum, but it may also mean that both come from the same survey; the viewer shows no survey date, and S10 says the SonarChart keeps drying areas from the Hydrographic Office and interpolates the contours below (so SonarChart is not fully independent of older chart data). 6. Navionics soundings: 16 soundings on seabed inside the model grid (4 inside the plotted survey area, 12 in the spline-extrapolated area): model minus Navionics mean +0.06 m, sd 0.49 m, r.m.s. 0.48 m (survey area: mean +0.41 m, sd 0.41, n = 4; extrapolated area: mean -0.05 m, sd 0.47, n = 12). The extrapolation is therefore good to about 0.5 m over 100-150 m beyond the survey; the largest single differences (+1.0 m and -0.9 m) are near the reef toe and at the edges. 7. Design plan: Mead Fig. 3a gives a design relief of crest about 0 m (colour bar saturates) over a seabed of -2.0 m (east) to -5.0 m (west), and -3.9 m / -3.1 m at the two ends of the long axis (soundings E and F on the annotated figure); compatible with the survey seabed -3.0 to -3.3 m west of the reef (Oct 2009) and -3.2 to -3.9 m at the shoreward end. 8. Tide: Table 1 reproduces the printed 1.76 m MHWS-MLWS range (E7); S2 quotes a maximum spring range of 1.96 m (different definition, not used).

5. Uncertainty

Propagation (independent errors, first order): sigma_f^2 = sum_i (df/dx_i)^2 sigma_i^2.

  • Crest in the model frame (E6): z_crest,MSL = h_c - D, sigma^2 = sigma_hc^2 + sigma_D^2, with sigma_hc = 0.3 m (A6), sigma_D = 0.1 m (A4): sigma = 0.32 m. Crest below LAT: d_LAT = -(h_c - z_LAT), so the crest stands 0.56 m above LAT (d_LAT = -0.56 m), sigma^2 = sigma_hc^2 + sigma_LAT^2, sigma_LAT = 0.05 m (table precision): sigma = 0.30 m.
  • Reef height at a point: H = z_c - S, sigma_H^2 = sigma_hc^2 + sigma_read^2 + sigma_tps^2, with colour read 0.2 m and interpolation under the reef 0.3 m (TPS ring r.m.s. 0.02 m, but the pre-reef seabed is unobserved): sigma_H = 0.47 m on a mean height of 3.2 m (median surveyed relief 2.3 m, maximum 4.1 m, after damage and smoothing). The datum risk is separate: if the survey zero were ODN, S would be 1.4 m higher in the model frame and H smaller by 1.4 m (absolute heights of the survey shift, relief of the survey does not).
  • Seabed depth at a point inside the survey: sigma = 0.2 m (colour read) plus the plot's own interpolation; extrapolated: 0.5 m from the Navionics comparison (validation 6), growing with distance.
  • Volume: (sigma_V/V)^2 = (sigma_A/A)^2 + (sigma_H/H)^2 + (sigma_m)^2, with area +-5 % (1 m outline error on a 120 x 45 m field), height 0.47/3.2 = 15 %, slope 5 %: about 16 % (the sensitivity runs in validation 2 span -12 % to +14 %).
  • Outline: +-1 m on the west, east and south edges, +-1.1 m on the shoreward edge (S7); position of the whole frame relative to the true geography about +-5 m (Esri georeference, OSGB conversion).
  • Navionics: area +-10 % (pixel read, boundary smoothing), soundings +-0.05 m read, +-1 m in position.
  • Vertical exaggeration: affects only the picture. At e = 3 a height error of 0.3 m looks like 0.9 m; slopes, crest cover and volume look larger by e. Use e = 1 for any quantitative reading and for photo matching.

6. Confidence

Level: medium. Against the rubric: the plan shape is itself rated medium (area 60 % below a repeated "about 1 ha" in the literature, three plan-view sources agree with each other); the seabed is read from a real DGPS plot (+-0.2 m) and confirmed by 16 independent Navionics soundings (mean difference +0.06 m); the as-built crest is given by the designers and checked against the Oct 2009 profiles (+-0.3 m); tide levels come from a gauge table in the design paper and the datum offset from the national tide facility. What keeps it from "high": the zero of the survey plot is an assumption (A3), strongly supported but not stated by the authors (the text is garbled); the as-built flanks and the flat crest are idealised (A6, A7; the two-level "focus" and "wedge" sections of the design are not published); the beach and the pre-reef seabed under the reef are interpolated (A8, A10); no as-built survey grid exists in the sources, only profiles of October 2009.

7. Limitations and unknowns

Gap How it could bias the model What would resolve it Lior can supply
vertical datum of the Fig. 9 plot and of Navionics not stated all absolute heights +-1.4 m if wrong (relief unchanged) Rendle PhD thesis (Plymouth PEARL 412, bot-checked), CCO survey metadata, or the Navionics app datum setting Navionics app: depth readings and the datum / tide setting; the thesis via a normal browser
as-built plan not directly observed (outline from 2011-09-28) outline may differ by a few m on the damaged offshore half a 2009-2010 aerial image Google Earth Pro historical imagery 2009-2010
crest height along the whole reef is the design value local crest heights +-0.3 m; "focus" and "wedge" sections have different heights Oct 2009 survey grid, thesis bag layout thesis, CCO data request
beach and surf line the model beach (y < 100) is extrapolated CCO beach profile, or Google Earth waterline at a dated image with known tide Google Earth Pro waterline in a dated image
Navionics survey date, drying height cannot tell what epoch the shoal shows Navionics app (tap on the drying area) Navionics app
no time curve of the tide, double high water not modelled the "level" is a static picture Bournemouth predictions (UKHO EasyTide) for the photo time tide table for the photo date
no bag texture photo matching of the surface texture is impossible; only silhouette and horizon container layout from the thesis thesis

See REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR.md for exact points and values to read.

SOURCES_3D - boscombe-surf-reef (3D model data sources)

Run started 2026-10-05

Step 0 - inputs read (2026-10-05)

  • Read: common.md, model_3d.md briefs; shape.json (status verified, confidence medium), METHOD.md, VERIFY.md, sources.md, 07_scale/reefs/boscombe-surf-reef.md (+footprint.json), card/dossier.
  • Both ICCE papers re-downloaded to the scratchpad (text extracted with pdftotext) to read datum / depth / tide statements myself:
  • Mead S., Blenkinsopp C., Moores A., Borrero J. (2010) ICCE, art. 1352 - https://icce-ojs-tamu.tdl.org/icce/article/download/1352/pdf_106
  • Rendle E., Davidson M. (2012) ICCE, art. 6794 - https://icce-ojs-tamu.tdl.org/icce/article/download/6794/pdf_441/27535

Step 1a - text facts found (quotes <= 25 words)

  • Mead 2010 p.1-3: "The tidal range between MHWS and MLWS at Bournmouth is 1.76 m." Table 1 "Water levels at Boscombe (m, ACD)": HAT 2.59, MHWS 2.21, MHWN 1.67, MLWN 1.17, MLWS 0.45, LAT -0.06. Gauge on Bournemouth Pier.
  • Mead 2010 p.2-3: "The design has a crest height of 0.5 m above chart datum." / "This design was set in water depths of 3-5 m (CD)" (Fig 3a).
  • Mead 2010 p.8: settlement "0.5 m or less, as specified in the design" (reduces crest height).
  • Mead 2010: 54 containers, diameters 1-5 m (text also "1 to 4 m"), lengths 15-70 m; lower layer first (2008), upper layer 2009; "dual level reef with a focus section ... and a wedge section".
  • Rendle 2012 p.3: "Situated 225 m offshore in 2.7 to 5 m depth"; "maximum spring tidal range of 1.96 m"; 32 containers "in two layers".
  • Rendle 2012 p.8: "MSL is equivalent to Chart Datum, Newlyn" (garbled; 0 m contour in Fig 10 = shoreline), "-3.5 m contour has eroded near the base of the reef".
  • Rendle 2012 Fig 9 profiles: Depth axis crest +0.5 ... +0.8 m, toe about -3 m, seaward end about -5 m (see Step 2).
  • NTSLF "Chart datum and ordnance datum" table (https://ntslf.org/tides/datum): "Bournemouth | -1.40 m" = chart datum is 1.40 m BELOW ordnance datum (ODN). So height ACD = height ODN + 1.40 m.
  • Herbert R.J.H. et al. 2017 PLoS ONE (https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0184100): "shallow water (0-5 m Chart Datum)"; "upper section is exposed on low spring tides"; "220 m offshore and 210 m east of Boscombe Pier".
  • Unverified (search-engine snippet only; full text not reachable, Plymouth PEARL thesis URL returned 403 to curl/WebFetch, academia.edu / ResearchGate 403): "The final crest height of Boscombe ASR was 0.5 m higher than the final design height" (Rendle thesis, 2016?). NOT used for numbers; listed as a risk (crest could be up to +1.0 m CD).
  • Wikipedia and Raised Water Research pages: no depth/crest/datum data (checked 2026-10-05).

RESUME 2026-10-05 ~13:20 (second run; the first run was cut off after the survey colour-read scripts)

  • Found at resume: SOURCES_3D.md (step 0, 1a text facts), scripts\canon.py (OSGB<->canonical conversion), survey_read.py (colour bar -> depth for Rendle Fig 9 left panel), survey_grid.py (resample to canonical 1 m grid, saved _survey_can_1m.npz, NOT yet registered to the satellite outline), annotated\ empty, no model.js / index.html.
  • Papers re-downloaded into the scratchpad by this run to re-read datum statements (see below).

Step 1 - FEASIBILITY (second run, 2026-10-05)

Decision: BUILD. a, b and d are sourced (details below); c and e are sourced/estimated with stated assumptions.

a. PLAN SHAPE - sourced: shape.json canonical polygon (verified 2026-10-05; 25 vertices, 4,042 m2, traced on Esri Wayback 2011-09-28). Frame: x alongshore (bearing 83.4), y offshore (bearing 173.4), origin on the 2011-09-28 surf line; reef nearest edge y = 181 m, far edge y = 276 m. b. CREST ELEVATION - sourced, in two independent ways: - Designers: Mead et al. 2010 p.2 "The design has a crest height of 0.5 m above chart datum" and "raise the crest to a level above mean low water springs" (MLWS = 0.45 m ACD). Settlement "0.5 m or less". - April 2011 DGPS survey grid read from Rendle & Davidson 2012 Fig 9 (colour bar): crest zone about -0.5 .. +0.4 m (see Step 3 numbers), SE (shoreward) end highest; the 2009 profiles in Fig 9 lower panels show crest +0.2 .. +0.8 m (Oct 2009), and the April 2011 along-axis profile shows the damaged 70 m container as a -1.2 .. -2 m trough. c. HEIGHT ABOVE SEABED / SIDE SLOPES - sourced from the survey (relief = survey minus ambient seabed) and the Fig 9 profiles (flanks about 1:2 to 1:3 on the steep sides); two layers of geotextile containers, diameters 1-5 m, 15-70 m long (Mead 2010; Rendle 2012). d. SEABED - sourced: April 2011 DGPS bathymetry (Channel Coastal Observatory / Bournemouth BC) plotted in Rendle & Davidson 2012 Fig 9, read into a depth grid; covers y = 100..305 m of the canonical frame (parallelogram). Seabed -1.4 m (y 100) to -4.8 m (y 300) in the survey datum. Outside the survey (beach y < 100, corners, y > 305) the model EXTRAPOLATES and says so. EMODnet (115 m cells, LAT) used only as a coarse datum check (below). GEBCO not used. e. WATER LEVELS - sourced: Mead 2010 Table 1 (m ACD): HAT 2.59, MHWS 2.21, MHWN 1.67, MLWN 1.17, MLWS 0.45, LAT -0.06. MSL = 1.40 m ACD estimated (NTSLF: Bournemouth chart datum is 1.40 m below Ordnance Datum; ODN is about MSL; mean of the four Table-1 mean levels = 1.375). Model z = 0 at MSL, so z(MSL frame) = z(ACD) - 1.40.

Datum of the Fig 9 survey (the weakest link) - reasoning, 2026-10-05

  • Rendle 2012 p.8 says "In the UK, mean sea level (MSL) is equivalent to Chart Datum, Newlyn ... (0 m contour in Fig. 10)" - garbled (chart datum is NOT MSL); it concerns the beach 0 m contour, and could mean Ordnance Datum Newlyn (CCO beach surveys use ODN).
  • Evidence the reef survey depth axis is Chart Datum: (1) the 2009 crest in Fig 9 is +0.4 .. +0.8 and the designers' crest is +0.5 m ACD (a 1.4 m ODN offset would put the crest 1.4 m above the design); (2) Rendle p.3 "225 m offshore in 2.7 to 5 m depth" and Mead "water depths of 3-5 m (CD)" match the survey seabed at the reef (-3 .. -5); (3) Herbert 2017: upper section exposed on low SPRING tides = crest +0.5..+0.8 ACD, not +1.9 ACD; (4) EMODnet (LAT) is deeper than the survey by about 1.5 m, not 3 m (check below).
  • Decision: survey datum = Chart Datum (ACD). The viewer keeps an "alternative datum" switch (survey zero = ODN ~ MSL) so the effect of being wrong can be seen. Flagged in provenance as estimated, uncertainty +-1.4 m (all absolute heights; relief unaffected).

EMODnet coarse check (WMS GetFeatureInfo, layer emodnet:mean, retrieved 2026-10-05)

  • https://ows.emodnet-bathymetry.eu/wms (GetFeatureInfo). Cells ~115 m, values in m relative to LAT. Along the shore normal through the reef (canonical x = 0): y 100-200: -3.99 m; y 220-320: -5.62 m; y 340-440: -7.05 m; beach y -20..80: +0.14 m. Survey (April 2011, as ACD): y 100-200 about -1.4..-2.5; y 220-300 about -3 .. -4.8. EMODnet is deeper by 1.3-1.7 m (older / smoothed, pre-nourishment data probable), which is closer to the CD reading than to ODN (3 m). Only used as a datum plausibility check, not for values.

Registration of the survey grid to the satellite outline (computed 2026-10-05)

  • Survey Z (colour read, converted OSGB -> canonical via the img1 georeference, scripts/canon.py) minus an ambient order-2 polynomial seabed = relief. Relief mask > 1.0 m covers 4,078 m2 vs the satellite outline 4,042 m2; IoU 0.90 with NO shift (best shift search +-30 m: 0, 0). So the survey grid is used UNSHIFTED. (The earlier 0.77 IoU / 8.5 m centroid offset in shape.json came from tracing the -2/-3 m colour edge, not from a misregistration.)

STEP 6 added by the orchestrator (2026-10-05, mid-run): 3d\METHODS_3D.md (academic methods note), 3d\docs.js (window.REEF_DOCS), a "Methods & sources" panel in index.html and a build_3d.py that regenerates model.js + docs.js. Will be delivered before finishing.

Step 2/3 progress (second run) - processing log

  • 2026-10-05: scripts/survey_read2.py replaces survey_read.py. Two fixes: (i) the old 'dark pixel' test (R+G+B < 200) also caught the dark-red (103,10,15) and dark-blue (4,2,139) ends of the jet colour bar, i.e. real crest / deep-water pixels, and inpainted them -> test is now max(R,G,B) < 90 (black section line / text only); (ii) pixels hidden by the black section line on the left map are taken from the right map (same surface, offset +469 px, -1 px by template match, SQDIFF 0.028). Result: colour-bar range now fully used (-5.30 .. +0.90 m), median colour distance to the bar 11.7 (RGB units), 95th percentile 20.
  • scripts/fields.py builds the grids (see METHODS_3D.md for equations). Key numbers (run 2026-10-05): TPS seabed fit rms 0.02 m on the decimated ring points; relief > 1 m covers 3,841 m2 (poly-ambient version 4,078 m2) vs satellite outline 4,042 m2; relief volume 9,573 m3 (April 2011 survey); idealised loft volume 13,644 m3 (stated 13,000); median relief inside the outline 2.3 m, max 4.1 m; crest max z = +0.68 m ACD at x=20, y=193 (SE, shoreward end).
  • Herbert et al. 2017 re-fetched 2026-10-05 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5604948/): "shallow water (0-5 m Chart Datum)"; "the upper section is exposed on low spring tides"; "located 220m offshore and 210m east of Boscombe Pier". riverlevels.uk Bournemouth page: "usual range of the Tide ... between -1.08m and 1.11m" above Ordnance Datum (centred +0.02 m ODN, supports ODN ~ MSL).

Step 2 - annotated sources (second run, 2026-10-05) - captions

All files in 3d\annotated\ ; private research copies; reuse rights of the underlying figures NOT cleared (authors' copyright / Esri-Maxar terms). 1. fig9_depth_read_map.png - Rendle & Davidson (2012) Fig. 9 left map (April 2011 DGPS bathymetry). Marked: colour bar (ticks y=55..244 px = 0..-5 m, bar top +0.93 / bottom -5.30 m), OSGB gridline anchors (E 411400 at x=147.3 px, E 411550 at 433.5; N 91000 at y=39.0, N 90820 at 235.3), the area read, depth contours of the colour read (0,-1,-2,-3,-4 m), the reef outline from shape.json projected into the figure, six soundings A-F (A crest +0.69 m, B seabed shoreward -2.02, C seabed offshore -4.77, D west -3.83, E east -2.82, F -1.62) and section S1. 2. fig9_profiles_read.png - Fig. 9 lower panels (4 CCO surveys, Oct 2009 - Apr 2011). Marked: design crest +0.5 m ACD line, Oct 2009 crest tops (+0.45 m across the reef, +0.65 m along the axis), April 2011 dip -1.95 m (lost container, 'depression in crest height of 2 m'), April 2011 along-axis trough -1.1..-2.2 m, seabed levels (-3.0..-3.3 m W of reef; -3.2..-3.9 m NE end), SW flank slope (2.0 m rise over 6-8 m = 1:3..1:4; steepest 2 m window 1:1.5). REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR - Boscombe Surf Reef 3D model (2026-10-05)

The model is built and usable as it is (confidence medium). The items below are what I could NOT read myself, or only partly. Each one says what I assumed meanwhile, so nothing is waiting on you. Coordinates are decimal degrees, WGS84 (lat, lon); I computed them from the verified outline and the model frame (x alongshore, y offshore, see METHODS_3D.md 3.1).

What I did read myself (so you do not need to repeat it): the Garmin Navionics web viewer (Nautical Chart and SonarChart, metres, zoom 18) - the old ChartViewer is gone, but maps.garmin.com/en-US/marine shows both layers without login; soundings and shoal areas are in annotated\navionics_*.png. The viewer does NOT state a depth datum or a survey date, and it prints no drying height.

A. Navionics app (phone / tablet), SonarChart or Nautical Chart, depths in metres

models.name: Bunbury Airwave
models.model_name: Bunbury Airwave: sand-slurry-ballasted rubber (Hypalon) bladder, as installed Dec 2019 - torn, not a working reef
models.state_short: As installed, December 2019: 12 m sand-slurry bladder, torn along a glued seam before completion (card verdict FAILED). Geometry only; it never operated as a reef. Removal, redesign and the 2025 granite proposal are not modelled.
models.state_full: Installed bladder (installation attempted December 2019: began the week of 9 Dec, seam tear spotted Fri 13 Dec at about 90 % complete), torn before completion - not a working reef
models.caption: Installed bladder (December 2019: install week of 9 Dec, seam tear spotted Fri 13 Dec), torn before completion - not a working reef. Card verdict: FAILED. Sand-slurry-ballasted Hypalon rubber, removed within days; no independent record of rideable waves. The developer's "In 2018" is contradicted by every dated 2019 report (Methods 2.1; this model uses December 2019). Shape drawn = symmetric-cap stand-in.

confidence.reason: MEDIUM, by the rubric in METHODS_3D.md section 6. The seabed comes from an airborne-lidar survey of this exact beach (smooth 1:24 slope), an independent Navionics chart agrees with it to 0.32 m RMS once its depths are read below LAT, and the tides are from a port table. The text-implied seabed (crest 1 m below low tide + 1.6-2 m height) is reached by the lidar at y = 42-50 m, inside the 30-50 m text range. Against that: the survey is from 2009, its 10 m cells cannot resolve the 12 m reef, the offshore distance is a 30-50 m text range (+-0.4 m of depth), and the crest depth, height and flank shape are text or estimates. Crest depth below MLLW is 0.69 +- 0.66 m (Monte Carlo over the position and height ranges), against 'about 1 m' in the text. The as-installed bladder was partly filled, unanchored and torn, so its true surface differs from the symmetric cap drawn.
confidence.reason_short: Seabed (2009 lidar, cross-checked by Navionics, RMS 0.32 m) and tides are sourced; reef height, crest depth and the installed shape are text-based or assumed, and the bladder never operated.

models.methods_html:
METHODS_3D - Bunbury Airwave (Bunbury Back Beach, Western Australia): three-dimensional model

Built 2026-10-05 by build_3d.py (numbers in this note are filled in by that script from shape.json, the reef card, data/lidar_*, and data/nav_transects.json; edit METHODS_3D.template.md, not this file). Companion notes: SOURCES_3D.md (running log of what was read where), REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR.md (what could not be read), annotated/ (the sources with the readings marked: lidar figures and N1-N4 for Navionics).

1. Summary

The model shows the Bunbury Airwave as installed in December 2019: a 12 m diameter bladder of Hypalon (synthetic) rubber with glued seams, partly filled with sand slurry (washed beach sand, 140-150 t by the developer's own figures), water and air, lying on the nearshore seabed of Back Beach, 30-50 m off the waterline, with the water surface at any tidal plane from LAT to HAT. It is not a rock reef and not a working reef: the installation began in the week of 9 December 2019, a diver spotted a tear along a glued seam on Friday 13 December when the bladder was about 90 % complete and not fully anchored, and it was removed within about three days. The card verdict is FAILED and stays so; the developer's page says "In 2018" and "wasn't a failure", but the year is contradicted by every dated 2019 report and no independent source documents rideable waves (section 2.1). The seabed is the WA Department of Transport airborne-lidar survey of 2009 (10 m grid), cross-checked against Garmin Navionics SonarChart contours I counted from the web viewer (RMS 0.32 m once its depths are read below LAT, the Australian chart datum); tides are the Port of Bunbury planes (GHD 2021). The footprint is the verified circle of shape.json; the height (1.6-2.0 m), crest depth ("about 1 m" at low tide) and profile are text-based, and the surface drawn is a symmetric spherical-cap stand-in because no cross-section of the installed bladder exists. Later events (removal, redesign, the 2025 granite proposal) are not modelled; they are in the viewer caption and in section 2.1. The 3D confidence is MEDIUM: the seabed and tides are sourced and independently cross-checked, but the reef geometry is text-based, the crest depth below MLLW is 0.69 +- 0.66 m (Monte Carlo over the position and height ranges) against "about 1 m" in the text, and the real bladder was partly filled and torn.

3. Methods

3.1 Coordinate frame and orientation

The model frame is the canonical frame of shape.json: metres, x alongshore toward bearing 12.32 deg true (NNE), y seaward toward bearing 282.32 deg true (WNW, x turned 90 deg anticlockwise), z up, z = 0 at mean sea level (MSL). (x, y, z) is right-handed; the viewer maps model (x, y, z) to three.js (X, Y, Z) = (x, z, -y), which is mirror-free. The origin O is the foot of the perpendicular from the site point on the fitted 0 m AHD contour of the 2009 lidar (MGA94 zone 50: E 372378.8, N 6311547.1); y = 0 is that contour (about the MSL waterline of 2009).

The contour was fitted to the zero crossings of the lidar along 201 grid rows (|north| <= 500 m): east = a + b north with a = 38.7 m and b = 0.2046 (relative to the site point; rms scatter 8.4 m). With t = (b, 1)/sqrt(1 + b^2) the unit vector along the contour and n = (-t_N, t_E) its seaward normal:

(E, N)_grid = O + x t + y n                                   (E1)
bearing_true = bearing_grid + gamma,   gamma = 0.754 deg   (PROJ, MGA94 zone 50 at the site)   (E2)
north in the model frame = (cos bx, cos by)                   (bx, by = true bearings of +x, +y)    (E3)

Orientation assumption (A1): +y is perpendicular to the 2009 0 m AHD contour. The Navionics 0 m line (green/blue edge) is tilted +2.4 deg against the model x axis (section 4, V9): slightly more than the +-2 deg contour scatter, which is plausible for two lines drawn 10 years apart.

3.2 Vertical datums and conversions

All elevations are held relative to AHD and converted to the model zero with the Port of Bunbury table (GHD 2021, Table 1: MSL = +0.1 m AHD):

z_MSL = z_AHD - (MSL - AHD) = z_AHD - 0.1 m                              (E4)
a depth d below datum D (D given in m relative to AHD):   z_AHD = D - d          (E5)
depth of a point at level L below a plane P (both m AHD):  d(L | P) = P - L        (positive = below)   (E6)
crest depth below plane P:                                  d_c(P) = P - (z_bed + H)                  (E7)

Tidal planes used (m relative to AHD; the model z is that minus 0.1): HAT 0.6, MHHW 0.2, MLHW +0.1, MSL +0.1, MHLW 0.0, MLLW -0.2, LAT -0.6 (LAT is the chart datum since 2009; in m above chart datum 1.3 / 0.9 / 0.7 / 0.7 / 0.6 / 0.5 / 0.1). In model z: HAT 0.5, MHHW 0.1, MHLW -0.1, MSL 0, MLLW -0.3, LAT -0.7 m. The range HAT - LAT is 1.2 m ("maximum tidal range of 1.2 m", "predominantly diurnal", GHD 2021). The DoT survey index gives LAT = AHD - 0.57 m for Bunbury (difference to the table: 0.03 m). The values are rounded to 0.1 m by the source; the gauge is the Bunbury Port inner harbour, assumed valid at Back Beach (A9). "Low tide" in the RWR crest-depth text is not defined; MLLW is assumed (A6) and LAT shown as the alternative (0.4 m lower).

3.3 Plan shape

The toe polygon (29 vertices, 112.1 m2) is read unchanged from shape.json (status verified, verified 2026-10-04, plan confidence medium, md5 f046605f97ddb20b3fb80a86d07b9a03). It is a circle seen at about 27 deg off nadir on the drone photo, rectified by stretching the minor axis; the 12 m scale is the text-stated diameter (so the agreement of 112.1 m2 with pi 6^2 = 113.1 m2, -0.9 %, is by construction). The photo shows a paler crescent on one rim (probably a slumped or damaged quadrant); excluding it would shrink the diameter by about 8 %. The viewer evaluates the outline as a radial function r(theta) about the polygon centre.

3.4 Seabed from the WA DoT 2009 airborne lidar (primary)

The BAG (10 m point grid, MGA94 zone 50, SW cell centre E361415 N6305610) was read once (stage 1, build_3d_lidar.py) and resampled bilinearly into the model frame on a 5 m grid, x = -150 ... +150 m, y = -40 ... +200 m (61 x 49 nodes):

z_AHD(x, y) = bilinear( grid, E1^-1 (x, y) )                                       (E8)

In the surf zone (y about -15 ... 35 m) there is no lidar return; 286 of 2989 nodes (9.6 %) are filled with the alongshore median profile P(y) (linear across the gap) plus a smoothed per-column offset o(x):

z_fill(x, y) = P(y) + o(x),   o(x) = 5-column moving average of median_y[ z(x, y) - P(y) ],  -40 <= y <= 80 m      (E9)

The profile statistics (median, 10th and 90th percentile over |x| <= 100 m, native sampling, 2.5 m in y) give, in m AHD: y = 20 m -1.10, 30 m -2.08, 37.5 m -2.58, 40 m -2.69, 45 m -2.97, 50 m -3.20, 60 m -3.62, 100 m -5.11, 150 m -7.12, 200 m -8.40. The mean slope for y = 30-100 m is 0.0409 (1:24.5), with no bar or trough within 200 m. The MLLW line (-0.2 m AHD) lies at y = 4.1 m, the LAT line (-0.6 m AHD) at 13.9 m and the MSL line at 2.4 m. The viewer meshes the 5 m grid; filled nodes are tinted. Contours (every 1 m AHD) are drawn from the filled grid.

The 12 m reef covers 1-2 native cells, so the seabed beneath it is a sloping plane, not resolved relief (A7). The survey is 10 years older than the installation (A8).

3.5 Reef surface (spherical-cap stand-in)

No cross-section of the installed bladder is published; the sources say "dome" (ABC 2019b), "a very subtle, flattened dome with a steeply angled back" (The Tradie Magazine 2019, seen in search text only), and, for the first bladder, "a bit of a skateboard ramp type thing" (Kennedy 2021). Default surface (A5): a symmetric spherical cap of base radius a = 6.0 m and height H (default 2.0 m, range 1.6-2.0 m, both design figures reported before the install). With R_s the sphere radius and t = r / r_rim(theta) in [0, 1] the normalised radial distance (so that the base follows the traced outline):

R_s = (a^2 + H^2) / (2 H)                                  H = 2.0 m: 10.00 m, H = 1.6 m: 12.05 m          (E10)
cap(t) = sqrt( R_s^2 - (a t)^2 ) - (R_s - H)                                                                       (E11)
z_surface(x, y) = z_bed(x, y) + 0.03 + cap(t)             (the cap follows the sloping bed; 0.03 m seats it)       (E12)
V = pi H (3 a^2 + H^2) / 6                                 H = 2.0 m: 117.3 m3, H = 1.6 m: 92.6 m3     (E13)
rim angle  theta_rim = asin(a / R_s)                       H = 2.0 m: 36.9 deg, H = 1.6 m: 29.9 deg  (E14)

An optional ramp asymmetry A (0-0.6) displaces the apex towards a chosen true bearing (steeper on that side); no source says which side was steep, so the default is symmetric. No fill, valves, hoses, anchors or the tear are drawn (A12). The default centre is y = 37.5 m (shape.json); the viewer presets 30, 37.5, 45, 49.1 m (Tracks: "approximately 45 metres off the low tide mark", i.e. 4.1 + 45) and 50 m (SurferToday 2019).

3.6 Navionics (Garmin Marine Maps) as an independent seabed check

Access. webapp.navionics.com redirects to Garmin's Marine Maps viewer (https://maps.garmin.com/en-US/marine/). In my own headless Chrome (a fresh temporary profile and a random free DevTools port, never the shared browser pane; the script src/navionics/capture_navionics.py terminates only its own process tree) the page loaded with no login, CAPTCHA or consent dialog; nothing was accepted or bypassed. The page's own key (a geohash of the site) and Leaflet setView centred the map on -33.3276, 115.6284 at zoom 18 (the maximum) and 17, with Chart type = SonarChart Maps (or Nautical Charts), Depth units = Meters, Seabed areas = Hide, Shallow shading 1 m (the metres default). The app states no depth datum and no contour interval. Screenshots (private research copies, "Not to be used for navigation") were analysed offline; they were re-captured after a port-isolation notice and are byte-identical.

Scale and geometry. Web-Mercator: res = 156543.034 cos(lat) / 2^zoom / dpr = 0.2495 m per pixel at zoom 18 with device pixel ratio 2. A model point maps to the image through the true bearings of the model axes (E3).

Counting. 9 shore-normal transects (alongshore offsets -120 ... +120 m, step 30 m) run from the site point along +y. Along each, band boundaries (green drying area, dark blue, light blue, white) and thin dark contour lines were located (runs closer than 2.5 m merged because depth digits cross some lines). Index n = 0 is the green/blue boundary (the 0 m contour), n = 1 the dark/light blue boundary, n = 2 the light blue/white boundary (the 1 m shallow-shading limit), n >= 3 the thin lines. The interval 0.5 m is inferred and checked against the printed labels (1, 1.5, 2, 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5, 5 ... 8.5 on successive lines); every transect has 17-18 lines, monotonic and mutually consistent. The Nautical Charts layer shows contours 0 / 2 / 5 / 10 m and spot soundings, and agrees with the SonarChart lines (2 m at s = 3.1 m and 5 m at 75.1 m from the site on the main transect, against 2.1 and 77.2 m in SonarChart).

Datum test. For the n-th line the depth is d_n = 0.5 n m below the unknown datum D, so the lidar elevation there must equal D - d_n (E5). For a candidate datum D_c the misfit is the RMS of z_lidar(y_n) - (D_c - d_n) over the lines with valid lidar (y >= 30 m, inside the 300 x 240 m grid, not gap-filled); the free-fit datum is the mean of z_lidar + d_n:

candidate datum z (m AHD) RMS, 9 transects (n=111) bias lidar - Navionics RMS, main transect (n=12)
LAT -0.60 0.32 -0.24 0.35
LAT (DoT index) -0.57 0.34 -0.27 0.38
MLLW -0.20 0.67 -0.64 0.73
MHLW +0.00 0.87 -0.84 0.93
AHD +0.00 0.87 -0.84 0.93

The free-fit datum is -0.84 m AHD (sd 0.20 m over lines; standard error 0.019 m if the lines were independent, which they are not). Result: the Navionics depths are below LAT (the Australian chart datum); MSL and AHD are rejected (RMS 0.87-0.96 m), MLLW is disfavoured (RMS 0.67 m, twice that of LAT) but not excluded by the lidar's own 0.48 m uncertainty alone. Sand mass versus cap volume (V8; the settled sand volume is the mass divided by the bulk density; at 1.6 t/m3 dry and 2.0 t/m3 saturated):

sand mass settled volume (1.6-2.0 t/m3) share of cap, H = 2.0 m (117.3 m3) share of cap, H = 1.6 m (92.6 m3)
140 t 70-88 m3 60-75 % 76-94 %
150 t 75-94 m3 64-80 % 81-101 %

At 150 t and dry bulk density the sand alone would just fill a 1.6 m cap (101 %), so either the density is higher, the dome was taller, or the round number includes water; the 7 % gap between 140 and 150 t is smaller than the density uncertainty (about 25 %) and changes no model input. The mean load of 150 t on the 113.1 m2 footprint is 1.33 t/m2 (about 13 kPa); not used by the model.

5. Uncertainty

Per input (1-sigma-like ranges, not statistical intervals; where only text exists I state my judgement):

input uncertainty basis
outline +-0.4 m outline reading; size from the text, not measured shape.json verification
centre offshore, y uniform over 30-50 m: sigma_y = 5.8 m text range (RWR 30-45, Tracks 45 from the low-tide mark, SurferToday 50)
lidar seabed sigma_lidar = 0.48 m BAG uncertainty layer (A10)
seabed change 2009-2019 sigma_change = 0.30 m judgement (A8)
tide planes sigma_tide = 0.10 m port-to-beach transfer and 0.1 m rounding (A9)
height H uniform over 1.6-2.0 m: sigma_H = 0.115 m text (A4)
crest depth in the text sigma_text = 0.30 m "about 1m"

Propagation (independent errors added in quadrature):

seabed under the reef   sigma_zb^2 = sigma_lidar^2 + (s sigma_y)^2 + sigma_change^2            s = 0.0409  ->  sigma_zb = 0.61 m   ((s sigma_y) = 0.24 m)    (E15)
crest elevation         z_c = z_b + H        sigma_zc^2 = sigma_zb^2 + sigma_H^2               ->  sigma_zc = 0.62 m                                                      (E16)
crest depth below MLLW  d_c = MLLW - z_c     sigma_dc^2 = sigma_zc^2 + sigma_tide^2            ->  sigma_dc = 0.63 m   (below LAT: the same, 0.63 m)           (E17)
reef height             H itself: 0.115 m (range 1.6-2.0 m); there is no as-installed measurement

A Monte Carlo check (40000 draws: y uniform 30-50 m, H uniform 1.6-2.0 m, seabed and tide errors Gaussian as above) gives a crest depth below MLLW of 0.69 m with sd 0.66 m (5th-95th percentile -0.41 to 1.78 m); 32 % of draws are at least as deep as the text's 1.0 m. Weighting the draws by the text ("about 1 m", sigma 0.30 m) puts the reef centre at y = 41.2 +- 5.4 m (the viewer's "set offshore so crest = 1 m under MLLW" button solves the same condition). At the default y = 37.5 m, H = 2.0 m the crest is 0.38 m below MLLW, which is 0.9 standard deviations shallower than the text's 1.0 m (combined sigma of E17 and the text): consistent.

So the crest is 0.38 m (H = 2.0) to 0.78 m (H = 1.6) below MLLW at the default position, with sigma_dc = 0.63 m. Below LAT the crest is -0.02 m (H = 2.0: the cap just reaches LAT) to 0.38 m (H = 1.6).

Vertical exaggeration VE multiplies every z (water, seabed, reef) and leaves x and y unchanged: tan(angle_apparent) = VE tan(angle_true); at VE = 5 the 1:24.5 bed looks like 1:4.9 and the 2.0 m cap looks 10.0 m high, with its rim angle 36.9 deg steepening to 75.1 deg. Camera angles read for photo alignment are only valid at VE = 1; the viewer forces VE = 1 in photo-match mode.

6. Confidence

MEDIUM. Rubric used (my extension of the plan-shape rubric in SHAPE_SPEC.md, which covers only the outline): high = built-state footprint from a survey or georeferenced image, crest and seabed from surveys at the site and mutually consistent within 0.3 m, position known to better than 10 m, a measured as-built surface; medium = all vertical inputs sourced and consistent within 0.5 m, with at most one of (the surface shape is assumed, the footprint is a design, position known only to +-50 m); low = two or more of those, or vertical uncertainty at least half the reef height. Against it: the seabed is sourced (lidar) and independently supported (Navionics, RMS 0.32 m below LAT); the tides are sourced and cross-checked (0.03 m); the text-implied seabed and the lidar agree to 0.22-0.62 m at the default position and exactly at y = 42.0-50.0 m, inside the text range; the footprint is a verified outline from a photograph of the installed bladder (plan confidence medium); the offshore position is known to +-10 m (sigma_y 5.8 m). The one assumed element is the surface shape (A5), which makes it MEDIUM rather than HIGH; the height (1.6-2.0 m) and crest depth are text-only and the vertical uncertainty of the crest depth (0.63 m) is below half the reef height (0.8-1.0 m) so it is not LOW. Two cautions keep it from being stronger: the survey is 10 years older than the install and its cells cannot resolve the footprint, and the real bladder was partly filled, unanchored and torn, so the cap drawn is a stand-in for a shape nobody measured. The plan confidence (medium) is separate from this one.

REQUESTS FOR LIOR - Bunbury Airwave (Bunbury Back Beach, WA), 3D model (2026-10-05)

What the model already has: tide planes (GHD 2021, checked against the DoT survey index), seabed (WA DoT 2009 airborne lidar, checked against the Garmin Navionics SonarChart contours I counted myself from the web viewer, RMS 0.32 m once depths are read below LAT), plan outline (verified circle, 12 m), reef height and crest depth (text). The bladder was removed in December 2019, so Navionics shows no structure and was used for the seabed only. What I could NOT read, and could not find anywhere online, is listed here. The model is already built with stated assumptions; each row says what it would change. Neither tool can show the structure itself except Google Earth historical imagery, and only if an image from 9-20 December 2019 exists (the nearest imagery I found at the site is 2016 and 2025).

All coordinates are decimal degrees, WGS84 (lat, lon). They are computed from the model frame (origin -33.32767, 115.62880 = the 2009 0 m AHD contour; +x = 12.3 deg true alongshore, +y = 282.3 deg true seaward). Points are on the model's alongshore line x = 0 through the site point unless stated; a depth reading at them is a valid seabed reading whatever the true reef position is.

A. Where exactly was the bladder? (largest geometric unknown: +-100 m alongshore, +-10 m offshore)

# tool exact lat/lon or place what to read datum / units to note why it matters for the model
A1 Google Earth Pro, historical imagery slider Bunbury Back Beach, centred on -33.3276, 115.6284, 30-50 m seaward of the waterline, just south of the Bunbury SLSC building (-33.3271, 115.6298) the date of every image from Dec 2019 to Jan 2020 (the bladder sat in the water about 9-16 Dec 2019 and was removed within about three days); if one shows the pale circle, drop a placemark on its centre and copy the lat/lon, note the image date and whether the tide looks low WGS84 decimal degrees; image date (day) fixes the position (now a text/satellite estimate, +-100 m alongshore, +-10 m offshore = +-0.4 m of seabed depth)
A2 Google Earth Pro, ruler (path) from the A1 placemark (or, if no image shows it, from -33.3276, 115.6284) to the water's edge in the SAME image, along the shore normal (bearing about 282 deg true) distance in metres and the bearing the ruler shows metres; image date and whether the sand is wet/dry at the edge the distance offshore (text 30-45 m / 45 m from the low-tide mark / 50 m; each 10 m moves the seabed depth by 0.4 m)
A3 Google Earth Pro, ruler from the SLSC building corner (-33.3271, 115.6298) to the A1 placemark distance (m) and compass direction metres; degrees true confirms "just to the south of Bunbury surf club" (Tracks 2019) and the model's alongshore position
A4 Google Earth Pro, historical imagery the point -33.32767, 115.62880 (the model's 2009 0 m AHD contour) in the imagery nearest 2009-2010 and in the 2025 image: ruler distance from this point to the water's edge along bearing 282 deg; the image date and tide state metres; sign (+ seaward) shows whether the 2009 shoreline (which defines y = 0 for every distance in the model) has moved (2025 Esri waterline is about 7 m from the 2009 contour at the site)

B. Seabed depth (cross-check of the 2009 lidar and of my contour counting)

Navionics app (phone/tablet, SonarChart layer ON, "Sonar Logging" and "Community Edits" as you normally have them; set depth units to metres and say so). Tap the point and read the depth label; if the app shows a date/time and a tide-correction note, copy it. The "expected" cell gives the 2009 lidar value and, where I have one, my contour reading from the Navionics web viewer (both as depth below LAT, in metres); if the app is on a different datum the difference tells us which.

# tool exact lat/lon what to read expected (model) datum / units to note why it matters
B1 Navionics app -33.32767, 115.62880 depth at the point (tap it; SonarChart layer on) about 0.9 m ABOVE LAT = drying (lidar 2009) metres (say if the app is set to feet); whether the app says the depth is 'chart datum' or 'tide corrected'; time of day the model's y = 0 line (2009 0 m AHD contour)
B2 Navionics app -33.32765, 115.62867 depth at the point (tap it; SonarChart layer on) about 0.1 m ABOVE LAT = drying (lidar 2009); 0.0 m (my Navionics contour reading) metres (say if the app is set to feet); whether the app says the depth is 'chart datum' or 'tide corrected'; time of day where Navionics draws its 0 m contour (green/blue edge)
B3 Navionics app -33.32762, 115.62848 depth at the point (tap it; SonarChart layer on) 1.5 m (lidar 2009); 1.2 m (my Navionics contour reading) metres (say if the app is set to feet); whether the app says the depth is 'chart datum' or 'tide corrected'; time of day near edge of the 30-50 m text range
B4 Navionics app -33.32760, 115.62840 depth at the point (tap it; SonarChart layer on) 2.0 m (lidar 2009); 1.8 m (my Navionics contour reading) metres (say if the app is set to feet); whether the app says the depth is 'chart datum' or 'tide corrected'; time of day the site point = the model default reef centre (y 37.5 m)
B5 Navionics app -33.32759, 115.62833 depth at the point (tap it; SonarChart layer on) 2.4 m (lidar 2009); 2.2 m (my Navionics contour reading) metres (say if the app is set to feet); whether the app says the depth is 'chart datum' or 'tide corrected'; time of day far edge of the RWR range
B6 Navionics app -33.32758, 115.62827 depth at the point (tap it; SonarChart layer on) 2.6 m (lidar 2009); 2.4 m (my Navionics contour reading) metres (say if the app is set to feet); whether the app says the depth is 'chart datum' or 'tide corrected'; time of day SurferToday distance; where the text-implied seabed is reached for H = 2.0 m
B7 Navionics app -33.32756, 115.62817 depth at the point (tap it; SonarChart layer on) 3.0 m (lidar 2009); 2.8 m (my Navionics contour reading) metres (say if the app is set to feet); whether the app says the depth is 'chart datum' or 'tide corrected'; time of day just seaward of the reef zone
B8 Navionics app -33.32748, 115.62775 depth at the point (tap it; SonarChart layer on) 4.5 m (lidar 2009); 4.3 m (my Navionics contour reading) metres (say if the app is set to feet); whether the app says the depth is 'chart datum' or 'tide corrected'; time of day offshore, where the slope is well defined
B9 Navionics app -33.32812, 115.62819 depth at the point (tap it; SonarChart layer on) 2.4 m (lidar 2009); 2.2 m (my Navionics contour reading) metres (say if the app is set to feet); whether the app says the depth is 'chart datum' or 'tide corrected'; time of day alongshore check (hypothetical reef centre 60 m south)
B10 Navionics app -33.32706, 115.62846 depth at the point (tap it; SonarChart layer on) 2.4 m (lidar 2009); 2.2 m (my Navionics contour reading) metres (say if the app is set to feet); whether the app says the depth is 'chart datum' or 'tide corrected'; time of day alongshore check (60 m north)
B11 Navionics app anywhere on this stretch, same hour as the readings the app's tide-station name and the predicted tide height at the time of reading (Settings > Tides & currents), and any statement of the chart datum LAT is my inferred datum (RMS test, METHODS_3D.md 3.6) m above chart datum settles whether the app depths are tide corrected and which datum they use (MLLW would be 0.4 m shallower than LAT)

C. As-installed shape (not found anywhere)

# tool place what to read datum / units why
C1 e-mail to Waveco (Troy Bottegal) / the City of Bunbury (Dec 2019 council papers) the installation record: dive log, photographs with a scale, as-installed height and which flank was steep the as-installed height (1.6 m or 2.0 m?), a cross-section, the fill level when the seam tore, the orientation of the "skateboard ramp" metres; MLLW / LAT / AHD the model draws a symmetric cap; this is the largest remaining unknown in the reef surface
C2 e-mail to Raised Water Research (they published the drone photo and the Dec 2019 tear photos) the original, un-cropped drone frame(s) or video with metadata the date/time, altitude and any scale object - gives the plan scale independent of the 12 m text value
C3 WA Department of Transport (bathymetry) a survey of Back Beach after 2009 (the index lists only 2009 lidar at the open coast) whether a newer grid exists AHD or LAT replaces the 10-year-old seabed

D. Not needed from you

Tide planes (GHD 2021 table, cross-checked with the DoT index), the lidar, the card dates (December 2019, not 2018): done. No Haifa / Israel tide preset (local tides only).

lifecycle.event: Waveco's crowd-funding campaign (Kickstarter) fails; nothing deployed. The only 2018 events found.
ABC: the Airwave is set to be installed in November 2019.
Tracks: first live trial planned for mid-November at about 45 m offshore; the crowd-funding was 'last year'.
Raised Water Research: construction half-way.
Tracks: 12 m diameter, 1.6 m tall at the highest point; live trial 'in the next couple of months'.
Installation week (from Mon 9 Dec): slurry pump and hoses on the beach (7 Dec, forum observer); three divers and a boat.
A diver spots the tear along a glued seam: bladder about 90 % complete, not fully anchored. THIS INSTALLED, TORN STATE IS WHAT THE MODEL SHOWS (geometry only).
Tear reported (ABC, RWR, The Inertia, SurferToday). Bottegal: unexpected deep swell and undertow.
Bladder removed from the water (reports range from about 5 hours to 3 days).
Second prototype planned for December 2020 (about A$300,000 more needed); not confirmed built.
Tracks: Bottegal 'readily admits' the first trial was a failure; sand pumped too heavily into one quadrant; redesign with welded compound, only tank-tested.
Bunbury Mail: Bottegal says 'not a failure'; glued Hypalon seams; a lone 0.75 m wave seen (developer's account only); back in the water 'by Summer 2024'.

Waveco's Bunbury proposal is a granite (rock) reef, not the rubber Airwave. The About page (last modified 2025-12-22) says 'In 2018 ... successfully created peeling waves ... wasn't a failure' (year contradicted, waves not independently supported).

models.model_name: Palm Beach Reef (Palm Beach Artificial Reef, Gold Coast, Queensland)
models.state_short: As built, rock placed May-September 2019 (certified September 2019); no later works, damage or renewal found (searched 2026-10-05).
models.state_full: As built (rock placed May-Sept 2019, certified Sept 2019). No later works, damage or renewal found (monitoring to 2023: stable; rock visible on Esri imagery of 2025-12-01). Contour lines from the Bluecoast/Nearmap aerial of the completed reef (image undated, Sept 2019 - Sept 2020).

confidence.reason: Plan, crest level (-1.5 m MSL) and tide planes are sourced; seabed depth and reef height are inferred (no surveyed value read) from the Garmin Navionics chart and the aerial's unlabelled contour lines, which agree to 0.27 m on average (sd 0.55 m) - but the council register gives a taller reef (5 m, 33,000 m3) than the model (3.9 m, 22000 m3).
confidence.reason_short: Plan, crest level (-1.5 m MSL) and tide planes are sourced; seabed depth and reef height are inferred from the Navionics chart and the aerial's contour lines (they agree to 0.27 m), and the council register gives a taller, larger reef (5 m, 33,000 m3) than the model (3.9 m, 22,000 m3).

models.ve_note: Apparent slope = atan(v tan beta): the 1:12 flank looks like 1:12/v; the apparent reef height is v x H.

caveats.q: Volume and height vs the council register
caveats.model: envelope 22,000 m3; crest height above the seabed 3.9 m (max 4.17 m)
caveats.stated: City of Gold Coast asset register VOLUME 33,000 and HEIGHT_M 5 (units and reference not stated); 25,000 m3 'quarried rock' (ICM / Salyer 2024); 60,000 t placed (EPW 2020)
caveats.diff: -11,000 m3 (-33 %) and -1.1 m (-22 %) vs the register
caveats.reason: Not explained: the register may carry design or pay-line quantities, rock below the original seabed (toe trench, settlement), or the contour interval may exceed 0.5 m on the crest side. The register volume is reproduced only with a seabed 1.0 m deeper than all independent seabed evidence. 60,000 t / 33,000 m3 = 1.82 t/m3 is a normal placed-rock bulk density.
caveats.resolve: City asset team (meaning of HEIGHT_M and VOLUME); as-built multibeam / Design Reference Report
caveats.ids: s1; n1; s7; Gold Coast report 5.3
ev: The model envelope is 33 % below the register envelope.
The register's 5 m / 33,000 m3 lies 2.0 sigma (height) and 1.8 sigma (volume) above the model.

caveats.q: Datum: AHD vs MSL and the tide planes
caveats.model: z_MSL = z_LAT - 0.88 (Gold Coast Seaway planes)
caveats.stated: concept crest '-1.5 m AHD' vs built '1.5 m below MSL'; MSQ: AHD is 0.760 m above LAT at the Seaway benchmark (MSL = AHD + 0.12 m); Palm Beach interpolated MSL - LAT about 1.0 m (0.88-1.09)
caveats.diff: 0.12 m (AHD vs MSL); crest about -0.50 m LAT instead of -0.62 m LAT if MSL - LAT = 1.0 m
caveats.reason: MSQ has no Palm Beach row (the Seaway is 18 km away, Snapper Rocks 10 km with MSL 1.09 m above LAT). The earlier METHODS note calls the AHD offset unverified; the Gold Coast bathymetry report (2026-10-06) verified it at the Seaway benchmark.

caveats.q: Seabed and reef surface are inferred, not surveyed
caveats.model: seabed from the Navionics SonarChart; surface from 10 unlabelled aerial contour lines at an assumed 0.5 m interval
caveats.stated: contour interval regressed 0.459 +- 0.003 m (formal); toe elevation vs chart seabed -0.27 m (sd 0.55 m); pre-reef City survey profile (Mortensen 2015 Fig. 6) agrees with the chart to 0.2-0.3 m RMS after the LAT to AHD/MSL shift; City DTM has no open-coast seabed
caveats.diff: interval +9 % (assumed 0.5 vs 0.459); toe 0.27 m deeper than the chart
caveats.reason: With a 1.0 m interval the seaward toe would be at -12.5 m, 5 m below the chart. Absolute depth and height are +-0.5 m; no surveyed depth value was read.
caveats.resolve: As-built multibeam (City of Gold Coast); Navionics app readings A1-A7
ev: With 1.0 m the seaward toe would be at -12.5 m MSL, 5 m below the chart.

models.methods_html:
METHODS_3D - Palm Beach Reef (Gold Coast, Queensland): three-dimensional model

Model files: model.js, index.html, docs.js; regenerated by contours_s7.py, navionics_capture.py, navionics_isolines.py, build_3d.py (which calls write_provenance.py), annotate_3d.py, render_previews.py. All numbers below are read from validation_3d.json (written by build_3d.py). Source log: SOURCES_3D.md. Items the author could not read: REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR.md.

1. Summary

The model shows the Palm Beach artificial reef (a submerged basalt/greenstone rock mound, 162 x 91 m, 11,989 m2 in the model grid, about 225-374 m off the beach at 19th Avenue) as built in May-September 2019; no later works, damage, loss or renewal were found (monitoring papers to 2023 report a stable structure; the rock is visible on Esri imagery of 2025-12-01), so no second state is modelled. The plan outline, the crest outline (59.2 x 5.9 m) and the crest level (-1.5 m below mean sea level) are sourced; the tide planes come from Maritime Safety Queensland. The seabed and the rock surface are inferred: the seabed from the Garmin Navionics SonarChart (read in a headless browser by the author; datum not stated, tested to be LAT), and the rock surface from the 10 unlabelled contour lines drawn on a Nearmap aerial of the finished reef (interval assumed 0.5 m, confirmed independently to within 10 % by the Navionics seabed). The two inferences agree to 0.27 m on average (standard deviation 0.55 m, 427 points) but no surveyed depth value was read. confidence_3d = medium: the geometry is good enough for camera-angle estimation (plan +-1-2 m, crest level +-0.2 m, seabed and reef height +-0.5 m), but the council's asset register (HEIGHT_M 5, VOLUME 33,000) describes a reef 20-33 % larger than the model (crest height 3.9 m, envelope 22,000 m3), and that gap is unresolved.

2. Data sources

Full citations are in section 8. "Resolution" is the practical resolution for this site.

id source what it contributed resolution / date
s1 City of Gold Coast (2026), Artificial Reef layer toe outline (asset polygon, 154 vertices), attributes HEIGHT_M 5, VOLUME 33000 (units not stated; TOP/BASE_REDUCED_LEVEL empty) polygon +-0.5 m vs aerial; layer last edited 2026-10-03
s7 Bluecoast Consulting Engineers (c. 2020), Nearmap aerial with contour lines scale (8.50 px/m from the 0-25-50 m bar), north (arrow), toe outline, crest slot, 10 unlabelled contour lines 0.1176 m/px; undated (after Sept 2019, before Sept 2020)

s8 Engineering for Public Works (2020) pp. 50-51 "1.5 metres below the average water level at its highest point", 160 x 80 m, 270 m offshore from 19th Ave, rock classes, 60,000 t text
